   - Should work with custom metrics passed via SDK

The toolkit ships as four packages that work together: 28 29 - `frai` – the command-line app with ready-to-run workflows. 30 - `frai-core` – the reusable SDK that powers the CLI and any custom integrations. 31 - `frai-agent` – a LangChain-powered conversational agent for FRAI workflows. 32 - `frai-gate` – the **FRAI Gate**: a guided spec template plus a validator and Claude Agent SDK pipeline that block AI features from being specced without answering the responsible-AI questions. (The matching agent skill lives in [frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills).) 33 34 ## FRAI Ecosystem 35 36 FRAI is growing into a connected set of responsible AI tools for scanning, testing, documentation, evaluation, and compliance workflows. 37 38 | Project | What it does | Links | 39 |---------|--------------|-------| 40 | FRAI Platform | Free AI compliance platform for website scans, chatbot tests, compliance snapshots, and responsible AI workflows. | [Website](https://www.frai.cc/) | 41 | FRAI CLI / SDK | Open-source CLI and reusable SDK for responsible AI docs, code scanning, RAG indexing, evaluations, and governance workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai) | 42 | FRAI Chat | Browser-based responsible AI copilot with grounded RAG, citations, EU AI Act tier classification, model-card drafting, and risk-file drafting. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-chat) · [Live demo](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-chat/) | 43 | FRAI Benchmark | Open-source safety and compliance benchmark with a model registry, test suites, automated runs, and an interactive leaderboard. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-benchmark) · [Leaderboard](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-benchmark/) | 44 | FRAI Judge | Evaluation companion for judging AI outputs and supporting responsible AI review workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-judge) | 45 | FRAI Skills | Agent skills for responsible AI engineering - the FRAI Gate spec workflow for AI coding agents (`npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills`). | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills) | 46 47 ### Short Answer 48 - `frai-core` is the library/SDK. It wraps `frai-core` to deliver an end-user experience with no coding required. 50 51 ### Why Keep Both? 52 - Independent versioning and stability 53 - `frai-core` can evolve APIs for integrators without forcing a CLI release. 54 - `frai` can improve UX/commands without breaking programmatic users. 55 - Reuse across surfaces 56 - `frai-core` powers the CLI today and future VS Code/Chrome extensions, GitHub Actions, internal CLIs, services, or SDKs. 57 - Smaller, focused installs 58 - Operators install the CLI. 59 - Builders install only the core library they need. 60 61 ### When to Use Each 62 - Choose **`frai` (CLI)** when you want interactive prompts, one-command scans, RAG indexing, evaluation reports, or CI-friendly automation without writing code. 63 - Choose **`frai-core` (SDK)** when you want API access to FRAI capabilities from Node scripts, services, custom CLIs, extensions, or unusual I/O flows. 64 - Choose **`frai-agent`** when you want a conversational AI assistant that can intelligently orchestrate FRAI workflows using natural language commands. 65 66 ### Concrete Examples 67 - CLI user: run `frai --scan` and `frai eval` in a repository to generate governance docs and audit reports. 68 - Library user: call `Documents.generateDocuments` from an internal portal to produce standardized docs, use `Scanners.scanCodebase` inside a GitHub Action, or embed `Rag.indexDocuments` inside a VS Code extension for grounded hints. 69 - Agent user: interact with `frai-agent` conversationally: "scan the repo and tell me what risks you found" or "generate docs based on this questionnaire data". 70 71 In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. 185 import inquirer from 'inquirer'; 186 import { Documents, Questionnaire, Scanners } from 'frai-core'; 187 188 const answers = await Questionnaire.runQuestionnaire({ 189 prompt: (questions) => inquirer.prompt(questions) 190 }); 191 192 const { checklist, modelCard, riskFile } = Documents.generateDocuments({ answers }); 193 const scan = Scanners.scanCodebase({ root: process.cwd() }); 194 const aiContext = Documents.buildContextForAITips(answers); It provides an intelligent assistant that can scan repositories, generate documentation, and answer questions about your AI features. 210 211 ### Getting Started 212 213 From the monorepo root: 214 ```bash 215 pnpm agent:frai "Scan the repository and summarize AI risks." 216 ``` 217 218 ### Interactive Mode 219 220 Launch a chat-style session: 221 ```bash 222 pnpm agent:frai --interactive --verbose 223 ``` 224 225 The agent supports two tools: 226 - **`scan_repository`** – Scans your codebase for AI indicators using FRAI's static detectors. 227 - **`generate_responsible_ai_docs`** – Generates `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md` from questionnaire answers. 228 229 ### Example Usage 230 231 Scan a repository: 232 ```bash 233 pnpm agent:frai "Scan the repo and tell me what AI-related code you found." 234 ``` 235 236 Generate documentation (with questionnaire answers): 237 ```bash 238 pnpm agent:frai "Generate the docs with these answers: { 239 \"core\": { \"name\": \"ReviewCopilot\", \"purpose\": \"assistant\" }, 240 \"impact\": { \"stakeholders\": [\"developers\"], \"impactLevel\": \"medium\" }, 241 \"data\": { \"sources\": [\"internal docs\"], \"retention\": \"30 days\" }, 242 \"performance\": { \"metrics\": [\"accuracy\"] }, 243 \"monitoring\": { \"strategy\": \"daily review\" }, 244 \"bias\": { \"mitigations\": [\"red teaming\"] } 245 }" 246 ``` 247 248 ### API Usage 249 250 ```ts 251 import { createFraIAgentExecutor } from "frai-agent"; Generate evaluation reports for model outputs.
- `--outputs <file>` *(required)* – JSON file with model outputs.
- `--references <file>` – JSON file with reference answers.
- `--report <path>` – output location (`frai-eval-report.json` by default).

### `frai finetune`
Fine-tuning governance helpers:
- `frai finetune template [--output <path>]` – write a governance template JSON (`frai-finetune-plan.json` by default).
- `frai finetune validate <plan> [--readiness]` – validate a plan and optionally print readiness checkpoints and summaries.

### `frai update`
Check npm for the latest `frai` release and print upgrade instructions.

---

## Using `frai-core` (SDK)

Install from npm:
```bash
pnpm add frai-core
```

`frai-core` exposes modular helpers that the CLI uses under the hood:
- `Questionnaire` – interactive question flows.
- `Documents` – generate checklists, model cards, and risk files.
- `Scanners` – static analysis for AI indicators.
- `Rag` – policy-grounded indexing utilities.
- `Eval` – baseline evaluation metrics and report writers.
- `Finetune` – governance templates, validation, and readiness scoring.
- `Config` & `Providers` – key management and LLM provider wiring.

Example: generate documentation programmatically.

```ts
import fs from 'fs/promises';
import inquirer from 'inquirer';
import { Documents, Questionnaire, Scanners } from 'frai-core';

const answers = await Questionnaire.runQuestionnaire({
  prompt: (questions) => inquirer.prompt(questions)
});

const { checklist, modelCard, riskFile } = Documents.generateDocuments({ answers });
const scan = Scanners.scanCodebase({ root: process.cwd() });
const aiContext = Documents.buildContextForAITips(answers);

await fs.writeFile('checklist.md', checklist);
await fs.writeFile('model_card.md', modelCard);
await fs.writeFile('risk_file.md', riskFile);
await fs.writeFile('scan-summary.json', JSON.stringify(scan, null, 2));
await fs.writeFile('ai-context.txt', aiContext);
```

Because `frai-core` is a regular ESM package, you can import only the modules you need and embed FRAI capabilities inside automation pipelines, CI jobs, or custom products.

---

## Using `frai-agent`

`frai-agent` is a LangChain-powered conversational agent that wraps FRAI scanning and documentation workflows behind a natural language interface. It provides an intelligent assistant that can scan repositories, generate documentation, and answer questions about your AI features.

### Getting Started

From the monorepo root:
```bash
pnpm agent:frai "Scan the repository and summarize AI risks."
```

### Interactive Mode

Launch a chat-style session:
```bash
pnpm agent:frai --interactive --verbose
```

The agent supports two tools:
- **`scan_repository`** – Scans your codebase for AI indicators using FRAI's static detectors.
- **`generate_responsible_ai_docs`** – Generates `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md` from questionnaire answers.

### Example Usage

Scan a repository:
```bash
pnpm agent:frai "Scan the repo and tell me what AI-related code you found."
```

Generate documentation (with questionnaire answers):
```bash
pnpm agent:frai "Generate the docs with these answers: {
  \"core\": { \"name\": \"ReviewCopilot\", \"purpose\": \"assistant\" },
  \"impact\": { \"stakeholders\": [\"developers\"], \"impactLevel\": \"medium\" },
  \"data\": { \"sources\": [\"internal docs\"], \"retention\": \"30 days\" },
  \"performance\": { \"metrics\": [\"accuracy\"] },
  \"monitoring\": { \"strategy\": \"daily review\" },
  \"bias\": { \"mitigations\": [\"red teaming\"] }
}"
```

# FRAI · Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence ![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/frai) ![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/frai) **Live platform:** [frai.cc](https://www.frai.cc/) ![FRAI website screenshot showing the AI compliance platform, compliance snapshot, and FRAI Guard overview.](assets/frai_cc_screenshot.png) FRAI is an open-source toolkit that helps teams launch AI features responsibly. In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. They overlap in capability on purpose but target different audiences and distribution needs. --- ## Getting Started with the CLI 1. Install the published CLI: ```bash npm install -g frai ``` 2. Configure your OpenAI API key (needed for AI-generated tips and evaluations): ```bash frai --setup ``` Keys can be stored per-project (`.env`) or globally (`~/.config/frai/config`). Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, I can see that a significant portion of the threshold infrastructure is already in place. The core logic exists in `thresholds.js`, the report generation supports thresholds, and the Markdown reporter includes a thresholds section. However, the CLI integration is missing, and there are some refinements needed for robustness.

## High-Level Implementation Strategy

### Current State Analysis
The codebase already has:
- ✅ `parseThreshold()` - parses "metric_id=0.9" format strings with validation
- ✅ `validateThresholds()` - validates parsed thresholds against evaluated metrics, handles null scores as failures
- ✅ `didAllThresholdsPassed()` - checks overall threshold status
- ✅ `generateReport()` - already accepts thresholds parameter and adds `passed` and `thresholds` fields
- ✅ Markdown reporter - already includes Thresholds section in output
- ✅ Comprehensive unit tests for threshold logic

**What's Missing:**
- ❌ CLI `--threshold` option support (repeatable)
- ❌ Exit code handling (0 if pass, 1 if fail, 2 for errors)
- ❌ CLI error reporting with valid metric IDs listed
- ❌ Support for custom metrics (METRIC_IDS is hardcoded)

### Key Architectural Challenges

**Challenge 1: Custom Metrics Support**
- `parseThreshold()` validates against a hardcoded `METRIC_IDS` list before evaluations run
- For custom metrics passed via SDK, this validation fails prematurely
- **Solution:** Move metric ID validation from parse time to validation time (after evaluations)

**Challenge 2: Helpful Error Messages**
- When a metric ID is unknown, we need to list available IDs
- These IDs come from evaluations, not from `parseThreshold()` 
- **Solution:** Defer metric ID validation, catch errors in CLI, extract available IDs from evaluations

**Challenge 3: Null Score Handling**
- Some metrics return `score: null` when data is insufficient (e.g., exact_match without references)
- **Solution:** Already handled—`validateThresholds()` correctly treats null as failed

### Implementation Order

#### **Step 1: Refactor thresholds.js for Custom Metrics**
**File:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-core/src/eval/thresholds.js`

- Remove hardcoded `METRIC_IDS` validation from `parseThreshold()`
- Change `parseThreshold()` to only validate format: `metric_id=number` with 0-1 range
- Update `parseThreshold()` to return just `{ metricId, min }` without knowing about available metrics
- Let `validateThresholds()` handle metric ID validation against evaluated metrics
- Export a helper function to extract available metric IDs from evaluations for error messages

**Why this order:** This is the foundation. Without this, custom metrics can't work, and the CLI can't provide helpful error messages.

#### **Step 2: Enhance Error Handling in thresholds.js**
**File:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-core/src/eval/thresholds.js`

- Add helper function `getAvailableMetricIds(evaluations)` to extract metric IDs
- Update `ThresholdError` to optionally include available metric IDs
- In `validateThresholds()`, when throwing for unknown metric, include available IDs

#### **Step 3: Add CLI --threshold Support**
**File:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts`

- Add `thresholds?: string[]` to `EvalOptions` interface
- Update eval command to accept repeatable `--threshold <metric>=<min>` option
- In `runEvalCommand()`:
  1. Parse each threshold string with `parseThreshold()` (catches format errors)
  2. Run evaluations
  3. Call `generateReport()` with parsed thresholds
  4. If `report.passed === false`, exit(1)
  5. If any parsing error, catch and report with available metric IDs, exit(2)
  6. On success, exit(0)

**Exit Code Semantics:**
- 0: All thresholds passed (or no thresholds specified)
- 1: At least one threshold failed
- 2: Usage error (malformed threshold or unknown metric)

#### **Step 4: Update Tests**
**Files:** 
- `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-core/src/eval/thresholds.test.js`
- `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js`

Add tests for:
- `parseThreshold()` with unknown metric ID (should NOT throw, format still valid)
- Custom metric validation in `validateThresholds()` with custom metric object
- Error message includes available metric IDs
- Null score handling in thresholds (already tested, verify coverage)
- CLI exit codes for pass/fail/error scenarios

#### **Step 5: Update TypeScript Interfaces**
**File:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts`

- Update `EvalOptions` to include optional `thresholds` field
- Add type safety for threshold parsing

### Sequence Dependencies

```
Step 1 (thresholds.js refactor) → Step 2 (error handling)
                                ↓
                        Step 3 (CLI integration)
                                ↓
                        Step 4 (Tests) + Step 5 (Types)
```

Steps 4 and 5 can run in parallel since they don't block each other.

### Non-Breaking Changes

These changes maintain backward compatibility:
- Without `--threshold`, exit code is always 0 (existing behavior)
- Reports without thresholds are unaffected
- SDK users can pass thresholds via `generateReport()`
- Existing tests continue to pass

### Testing Strategy

1. **Unit Tests (thresholds.js):**
   - Parsing accepts any metric ID in format (don't validate yet)
   - Validation against evaluations catches unknown metrics
   - Custom metrics work end-to-end

2. **Integration Tests (index.test.js):**
   - Thresholds + custom metrics
   - Null score failures
   - Report structure with thresholds

3. **CLI Tests (via manual/integration):**
   - `frai eval --outputs out.json --threshold exact_match=0.9`
   - Multiple thresholds: `--threshold exact_match=0.9 --threshold toxicity=0.95`
   - Error reporting with valid metric list
   - Exit codes (0/1/2)

- `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js` (no changes needed—already supports thresholds)

- `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js` (add CLI integration scenarios)

### `frai eval`
Generate evaluation reports for model outputs.
- `--outputs <file>` *(required)* – JSON file with model outputs.
- `--references <file>` – JSON file with reference answers.
- `--report <path>` – output location (`frai-eval-report.json` by default).
- `--format <json|markdown>` – output format (defaults to JSON). Markdown reports include human-readable summaries for review boards.
- `--threshold <metric=min>` – metric threshold to enforce (e.g., `--threshold exact_match=0.9`). Can be given multiple times. Exits with code 1 if any threshold fails, 0 if all pass, 2 for malformed thresholds. Valid metrics: `exact_match`, `toxicity`, `length_variance`.

### `frai finetune`
Fine-tuning governance helpers:
- `frai finetune template [--output <path>]` – write a governance template JSON (`frai-finetune-plan.json` by default).
- `frai finetune validate <plan> [--readiness]` – validate a plan and optionally print readiness checkpoints and summaries.

### `frai update`
Check npm for the latest `frai` release and print upgrade instructions.
